title: Yama, come and sit on the strewn grass

words.context: Yama, king of the Fathers; Bhāskara: «हे पितृराज»

words.meaning: the strewn layer (of sacred grass), the seat spread for the gods
words.context: Sāyaṇa on the Ṛgveda: «प्रस्तरं विस्तीर्णं यज्ञविशेषम्»

words.role: main verb of the first line

words.context: an ancient family of seers, counted among the Fathers; Bhāskara: «पितृविशेषैः»

words.gram: present middle participle, m. nom. sg.

sandhi.rule: a final m joins the following vowel
-āḥ before a voiced sound loses its visarga; u before a dissimilar vowel becomes v

morphology.note: an old instrumental of the pronoun (Vedic), ‘with this’, glossed by Sāyaṇa as एतेन.
the causative of √mad in the middle: ‘gladden yourself’, i.e. rejoice; Bhāskara: «मद तृप्तियोगे»

translation.literal: This strewn grass, O Yama, sit upon, in accord with the Aṅgirases, the Fathers. Let the mantras recited by the poets bring you here; with this offering, O king, rejoice.
translation.readable: Come, Yama, sit on this grass we have spread, together with the Aṅgirases, the Fathers. Let the words the poets recite bring you to us; take delight, O king, in this offering.

meaning: A call to Yama, king of the Fathers, to come with the Aṅgirases and sit on the grass spread for the gods, drawn by the poets’ mantras, and to rejoice in the offering. In the Navagraha sūktam it is the third mantra recited for Śanaiścara (Saturn), after śaṃ no devīḥ and prajāpate; the verse itself names Yama, and the witness names the adhidevatā and pratyadhidevatā of the graha together, without saying which mantra is whose.
in_the_rite: Step 7 (Śanaiścara), third mantra, before the salutation. The use of a Vedic verse for a graha belongs to the later gṛhya tradition; the commentary below speaks of the verse in its Vedic setting. In the Taittirīya Saṃhitā (TS 2.6.12.6) the corpus files the verse among the hotṛ’s mantras for the offering to the Fathers; it is also RV 10.14.4.

commentary.label: traditional
commentary.text: Bhaṭṭa Bhāskara reads Yama as the king of the Fathers and the Aṅgirases as a class of Fathers: «अङ्गिरोभिः पितृविशेषैः संविदानः ऐकमत्यं गच्छन्»; the mantras are those «कविभिर्मेधाविभिः आस्माकीनैः ऋत्विग्भिः शस्ताः».

commentary.label: traditional
commentary.text: Sāyaṇa, on the Ṛgveda verse: «हे यम अङ्गिरोभिः एतन्नामकैः पितृभिः संविदानः ऐकमत्यं गतस्त्वम्»; the last words he reads as a request on the sacrificer’s behalf: «एना एतेन हविषा तुष्टः मादयस्व यजमानं हर्षय».

notes.label: linguistic
notes.text: A triṣṭubh. The Taittirīya and the Ṛgveda (10.14.4) have the same words.
